Countdown: __next__ returns the current value and decrements it; raise StopIteration below 0.
Squares: To be reusable, __iter__ must return a NEW iterator each time.
Make __iter__ a generator: for i in range(self.n): yield i * i.
fibonacci: yield a, then a, b = b, a + b, n times.
positive_ints: Process one line at a time and yield.
try int(line.strip()) except ValueError: continue; yield only if > 0.
flatten_one_level: for group in groups: yield from group.
take: Never call list() on an infinite iterator.
make_tax_adder: The inner function remembers rate (a closure).
Define add_tax(price) inside and return it without calling it.
make_counter: The inner function must change an outer variable.
Declare `nonlocal count` inside the inner function.
trace: A decorator returns a wrapper function.
Use @functools.wraps(func) on the wrapper, print, then return func(*args, **kwargs).
require_minimum: The wrapper checks its first argument and raises ValueError if it is below minimum.
EventRecorder: __exit__ runs even when the block raises.
Append 'end' in __exit__ and return False so errors propagate.
cached_fib: Decorate with @functools.lru_cache(maxsize=None); base case n < 2 returns n.
totals_by_category: groupby only groups ADJACENT equal keys.
Sort by category first, then groupby with the same key and sum the amounts.
non_blank: Keep it lazy: a generator expression.
(line.strip() for line in lines if line.strip()).
chunked: Pull `size` items at a time from ONE iterator.
it = iter(iterable); while batch := list(islice(it, size)): yield batch.
running_total: The standard library already has this.
sliding_window: How many windows fit? len(values) - n + 1.
[tuple(values[i:i + n]) for i in range(len(values) - n + 1)].
once: Remember whether the function was called, and its result.
Use nonlocal variables in the wrapper; only call func the first time.
count_calls: Set wrapper.calls = 0 after defining the wrapper; increment it inside.
